# Brown University — RELAB (Reflectance Experiment Laboratory)

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | United States |
| **City** | Providence, RI |
| **Tier** | Extended (Tier II) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | Spectral libraries — reflectance (UV through far-IR) |

## Why it matters internationally

RELAB is primarily a **reflectance spectroscopy facility**, but it belongs
on any research map whose scope includes "reflectivity etc." Brown's DEEPS
department identifies RELAB as a research facility whose spectra provide
the **interpretive basis for remote compositional analysis**; the
laboratory operates UV–VIS–NIR bidirectional and near-/mid-/far-IR FTIR
spectrometers (to about 100 µm). RELAB has served for decades as a
NASA-supported multi-user spectroscopy facility whose data underpin
compositional interpretation of remote planetary surfaces. It represents
the truth that **reflectance and emissivity communities are deeply
connected** — Kirchhoff-related reasoning, spectral libraries, and
optical-constant interpretation cross these boundaries constantly.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant units

- **RELAB — Reflectance Experiment Laboratory** — NASA-supported multi-user
  facility at Brown, operating UV–VIS–NIR bidirectional and near-/mid-/
  far-IR FTIR spectrometers.
- **DEEPS — Department of Earth, Environmental & Planetary Sciences** —
  institutional home; presents RELAB as a core research resource.

### Radiative properties measured / curated

Spectral reflectance (UV–VIS–NIR bidirectional) · reflectance and
transmission in the near-, mid-, and far-IR.

### Capability envelope

- **Wavelength:** UV–VIS through far-IR; FTIR to **~100 µm**.
- **Methodology:** UV–VIS–NIR bidirectional spectrometer and near-/mid-/
  far-IR FTIR spectrometers; NASA-supported multi-user access for the
  external community.

### Signature infrastructure

- **RELAB spectra archive** — spectral reflectance and transmission data of
  Earth and planetary materials from visible through near-, mid-, and
  far-infrared wavelengths. A backbone dataset for planetary remote
  sensing.

### Application domains

- Planetary surface compositional interpretation
- Remote sensing spectroscopy
- Optical-constant interpretation and spectral-library reasoning

## Why Brown RELAB is a reference pole

The far-IR reach (to ~100 µm) and the breadth of materials in the RELAB
archive mean that a very large fraction of the published inversion chains
linking laboratory spectra to remote thermal-IR observations either
include RELAB data or rely on facilities like it. For the reflectance
half of the reflectance/emittance pair — which cannot be cleanly separated
from emissivity in any serious optical analysis — RELAB is one of the
indispensable US nodes.
